step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture shows an AWS-based cloud HPC orchestration system for computer-aided engineering simulations. The simulation input is loaded into Amazon S3, which triggers job scheduling via Amazon EKS. EKS provisions right-sized HPC compute nodes (EC2). During simulation execution, the HPC nodes stream logs directly to Amazon CloudWatch and output final results back to Amazon S3. CloudWatch triggers a downstream processing Lambda function upon detecting log alerts. This lower Lambda records execution status and duration into Amazon DynamoDB and publishes messages to Amazon SNS. Amazon SNS then triggers a second (upper) Lambda function for downstream asynchronous task execution.

graph.name: OnScale Cloud HPC Orchestration Architecture
graph.notes: An AWS architecture for scaling parametric engineering simulations using Kubernetes (EKS) for dynamic HPC node creation and Serverless (Lambda, SNS, DynamoDB) driven by CloudWatch telemetry for spiky workload handling.

edges.notes: S3 job submission schedules container provisioning in EKS.
EKS provisions right-sized HPC compute node.
HPC node writes encrypted simulation result outputs back to S3.

CloudWatch alert pattern triggers Lambda function for processing.
Lambda records job start/end timestamps and status in DynamoDB.
Lambda publishes event notification to SNS topic.
SNS notification triggers upper Lambda function for further downstream handling.
